exposure: targeted motor control interventions focusing on sternal and sacral alignment
outcome: spinal alignment (sternal angle, sacral angle, cervical and lumbar lordosis depths, thoracic kyphosis angle, pelvic tilt)
muscle activity (rhomboid muscles, serratus anterior muscle)
cohort: 32 pregnant women at 28-32 weeks of gestation, hospitalized due to the risk of preterm birth, who had low back pain lasting at least two weeks and the ability to walk and stand for 40 minutes.
finding: Targeted motor control focusing on sternal alignment significantly improved spinal alignment parameters, reduced pain intensity, and altered muscle activity (increased rhomboid, decreased serratus anterior) in pregnant women at risk of preterm birth with LBP.
